OTG: to ground in a host (A) plug, open in a device (B) plug
Configuration channel: the plug\'s orientation, the current, Power Delivery
Sideband use (alternate modes, e.g. DisplayPort\'s AUX)
Pins 1–4 are USB 2.0\'s; 5–9 are a USB 3.x A connector\'s extra row
The receptacle seen from the front. Row B is row A turned over, so the plug fits either way up. A USB 2.0-only C port has no TX, RX or SBU pins.
Pins 1–4 are USB 2.0\'s; 5–9 are a USB 3.x B connector\'s extra row, in the bump over them. Its pairs are the device\'s: it sends on SSTX.
Mini-A and mini-AB, now obsolete, have the same pins, with ID to ground
Micro-A (a host\'s, for OTG) has the same pins, with ID to ground
Pins 1–5 are micro-B 2.0\'s; 6–10 are the SuperSpeed part beside them, so a 2.0 cable still fits the left half
